newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore tanker fire kills crew member.
newsitem.headline: Singapore tanker fire kills crew member.

text.p: One crew member died and another was still missing after a fire on board an oil product tanker in Singapore harbour, police said on Thursday.

The fire on board the 26,909-dwt Ocean Trader broke out at 6.20 p.m. (1020 GMT) on Wednesday while the Singapore-registered vessel was berthed at an oil terminal operated by the U.S. oil company Mobil Corp on Pulau Pesek island.
The fire was brought under control at 7.45 p.m. (1145 GMT), the MPA said in a statement.
Mobil said the tanker was discharging condensate, a type of light crude oil, to the Mobil refinery when the fire began.

The offshore terminal is joined by a pipeline network to Mobil's 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery on mainland Singapore. The terminal has three berths for oil ships, and Mobil has three more berths on the mainland.
A Mobil spokeswoman said the fire on the Ocean Trader would not affect refinery operations. The ship had remained docked at the berth overnight, she said.
